apps.title: R apps with Shinylive builds
apps.disclosure_html: The site's publishing workflow exports these three R Shiny apps with Shinylive, so R starts inside your browser and the console takes several seconds to appear. The first visit downloads about 55 MB, shared with the other two apps on this site; later visits reuse the browser cache. It works best in Chrome or Edge; Safari support may vary. Exported and checked in headless Chrome locally; Safari and Firefox not checked. A Run in browser link appears on a card here only once a dated first-visit check is recorded for that app; until then each card links its read-only snapshot, its guide and the command that runs it in local R.

apps.title: Python in your browser (stlite)
apps.disclosure_html: Open an app to run it in your browser on bundled synthetic data (uploads are disabled in the public demo). The page is downloaded from GitHub Pages and jsDelivr, which see your IP address; the first visit downloads about 30 MB and Python starts in a few seconds. Not a validated or Part 11 system.

apps.title: JavaScript in your browser
apps.disclosure_html: The toolkit page makes no network requests and ships with a clearly fictional example. The playbook is its reading companion.

apps.title: Local R only
apps.disclosure_html: The find-hours app runs in local R (see its README); its guide and snapshot are static pages rendered with Quarto.

methods.title: Method transfers and operating characteristics
methods.intro: Two checks adapted from my research (the seeded-defect check and the within-sibling evaluation) and two operating-characteristics studies, all on synthetic data.

modules.title: A synthetic bioequivalence study, from sample size to CSR text
modules.summary: One synthetic 2x2 bioequivalence study taken from sample size and randomization through the SAP, ADaM (admiral), NCA (PKNCA), the ICH M13A analysis, rtables/tern tables, QC and CSR text.
modules.fact: QC is same-author re-derivation; define.xml and ADRG not authored.

modules.title: Sample size and randomization
modules.summary: PowerTOST sample size with a sensitivity grid, a blockrand randomization schedule with a balance check, and a protocol statistical-section excerpt with ICH M11 headings.

modules.title: SAP and mock shells
modules.summary: An estimand with the five ICH E9(R1) attributes, analysis sets, the ICH M13A model, BLQ and missing-data rules, and mock shells for the six executed tables.

modules.title: ADaM, specification and XPT
modules.summary: ADSL, ADPC, ADPP and ADAE with admiral, a specification in Pinnacle 21 layout read by metacore, SAS XPORT v5 files from xportr and Dataset-JSON copies.

modules.title: NCA, bioequivalence and TLFs
modules.summary: PKNCA NCA on actual times with BLQ kept as zero (ICH M13A), the ICH M13A bioequivalence model, six rtables/tern tables in RTF and HTML, three figures and a Quarto results report.

modules.title: QC by a second method
modules.summary: NonCompart against PKNCA for every NCA parameter, the BE model refit two other ways, and ADaM times, flags and adverse-event counts rebuilt in base R.

modules.title: CSR text, checked against the outputs
modules.summary: Section 11-style text with every number read from an output file, checked by the tlf_interpret number-grounding validator, with controls that show what it misses.

modules.summary: A worked Safety Review Committee example for a first-in-human dose-escalation study: the screening rules, a console that applies them, and the packet a committee would read.
modules.fact: Flags positions for a medical monitor and a committee; it does not adjudicate DLTs or Hy's Law cases.

modules.title: eCRF assist apps
modules.summary: Four Python apps: coding QC assist, de-identification review assist, participant risk screening (rule-based default thresholds) and central statistical monitoring. The evaluation reports its own failures: on held-out synthetic text, the de-identification stand-in left 108 of 308 identifiers readable (the full model path: 91 of 308).
modules.fact: In your browser: GitHub Pages and jsDelivr see your IP address; about 30 MB on first visit; uploads disabled. Not a validated or Part 11 system.

modules.title: Continuity and handoff toolkit
modules.summary: Turns a list of recurring statistical jobs into a coverage matrix, single-owner risks, per-job checklists and a printable handoff packet.
modules.fact: The page makes no network requests and ships with a clearly fictional example.

modules.title: What the harness catches
modules.summary: Programming defects from a list fixed in advance are planted one at a time in a throwaway copy, and each is recorded as caught (and by which gate or test), survived, equivalent or not applicable.

modules.title: Residual carryover and the ICH M13A 5% pre-dose rule
modules.summary: How the ICH M13A 5% pre-dose rule performs when washout is borderline: consumer risk, power and exclusions for washouts of 2 to 10 mean half-lives.
modules.fact: At 5 mean half-lives the rule drops 34% of participants; consumer risk 0.051 (MCSE 0.005).

modules.title: C-QTc hysteresis check
modules.summary: A prespecified check: the signed area of each participant's concentration-ddQTcF loop on residuals from the direct-effect model, with its operating characteristics.
modules.fact: Its test's standard error allows for the shared time-matched placebo mean.

modules.title: Within-sibling evaluation of the coding assist
modules.summary: With the neighborhood of terms given, does the coding assist pick the right member? An adaptation of the within-site permutation design from the AlphaGenome audit.
modules.fact: Within-set accuracy 0.909 (lab) and 0.861 (site) against a keyword rule's 0.970 and 0.819; both route to human coding.

modules.title: PK, NCA and bioequivalence sandbox
modules.summary: One synthetic 2x2 crossover (N = 40, seed 2026): eight ADaM-shaped domains, a one-compartment oral PK model, NCA, and the bioequivalence geometric mean ratio with its 90% confidence interval.
modules.fact: Re-running the script regenerates the committed output files byte for byte (checked with R 4.6.0).

modules.title: SAS TLF template library
modules.summary: 221 SAS programs across parallel, crossover, single-sequence, SAD and MAD designs: disposition, safety, PK, the BE mixed model, dose proportionality and accumulation.

modules.title: R TLF template library
modules.summary: The R twin of the SAS library: 221 scripts, one complete set per design, written with dplyr, tidyr, rtables, ggplot2, emmeans and lme4.
modules.fact: The R scripts parse under R 4.6.0 but have not yet been run on data.

modules.title: Validation harness and evidence ledger
modules.summary: Ten gates for a clinical-biometrics deliverable, run against this repository's own TLF libraries and synthetic ADaM data, with a seeded-defect check of what the gates catch.

modules.title: Number-grounding check for drafted TLF text
modules.summary: Checks drafted text for a table, listing or figure: the model never sources a number, and every draft is number-validated and human-gated.
modules.fact: Its self-test runs; the language-model step is a stub.

modules.title: SAS/R trial-monitoring automation
modules.summary: A deterministic, no-AI approach to trial monitoring in validated SAS and R: scheduled checks that detect and deliver pre-specified facts to a human, reproducibly.
modules.fact: It does not triage, narrate, or judge clinical meaning; humans own every decision.

modules.title: SAS/R monitoring and on-leave coverage wiki
modules.summary: Turns validated monitoring programs into a scheduled, self-escalating loop, so the trial keeps being watched and the tracker stays current while its owner is away.
modules.fact: Deterministic SAS/R, no AI required; all output routes to humans who decide.

modules.title: On-leave coverage playbook
modules.summary: Keeps deterministic SAS/R monitoring running when a job's owner is away, hands it off or leaves the study: the cover gets the updates, and escalation is automatic.
modules.fact: It detects, packages and emails pre-specified flags; a human makes every call.
